newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says it will focus on minerals.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says it will focus on minerals.

text.p: The managing director of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, John Prescott, said on Friday the resources giant would focus on minerals in the coming months.
"What we've seen is eight consecutive years of profit from minerals," Prescott said in a taped telephone message made available after the release of third quarter results.
"But in this particular quarter they had some difficulties that were partly one one-off," he said. Weather problems impacted on iron ore and coal during the quarter, he said.
The minerals division recorded a profit of A$105 million for the third quarter, up A$1 million from a year ago.

Despite the gain, BHP said higher costs and unfavourable product mixes at coal mines Australia and Indonesia combined with higher costs at its iron ore and manganese businesses weighed on group earnings, as did a stronger Australian dollar.
These factors were only partly offset by higher U.S. prices for coal and iron ore and increased shipments of iron ore during the quarter, BHP said.
BHP also said it would look to make improvements to its underperforming North American copper and metals divisions.

The Robinson mine in the United States and the Tintaya mine in Peru showed improvements during the quarter, although commissioining difficulties with the Kalamazoo, Arizona project adversely affected results, the company said.

The difficulties were more than offset by higher shipments during the quarter from the Escondida mine in Chile and the Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea, underpinning a 64.8 percent gain in third quarter profit to A$145 million for the copper division. BHP said its average realised price for copper shipped in the quarter was US$1.09 a pound.
This compares with an average London Metal Exchange spot price over the quarter of about US$1.07 a pound.
